props.title: Turning a Messaging House and Marketecture into One Clear Story
props.subtitle: Messaging house + marketecture
props.challengeSummary: You're asking about a messaging house and a marketecture: how to structure what you say and how to organize what you offer so both are easy to understand.

props.caption: The explainer video we made for Meta's business messaging story

props.title: Structure First, Then Message
props.content: A marketecture groups products the way customers think about them. A messaging house then carries one positioning idea down through each category to product-level proof points, so every team says the same thing at every level.

props.title: CrowdStrike: Applying the Power of a Great Marketecture
props.summary: We reorganized CrowdStrike's product portfolio through its customers' eyes into a new marketecture, and integrated it with the platform story into a keynote presentation.

props.title: Omnicell: Making Marketing and Sales Talk
props.summary: We built messaging hierarchies that connect Omnicell's high-level positioning to individual products, then used them to make first-call sales decks with illustrative metaphors and a two-page battle card.

props.title: Meta: Informed Messaging and a Unified Story
props.summary: We built an audience insight research report, narrative and messaging frameworks, an explainer video and industry-specific sales decks for Meta's B2B messaging products.

final.explanation: CrowdStrike is our direct marketecture work, and Omnicell shows the messaging layer that sits beneath that kind of structure. We haven't published a study that uses the term "messaging house", so Omnicell's messaging hierarchies and Meta's frameworks are the closest match. We'd start by agreeing the customer-facing categories, then build the messaging layers under them.
